<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD to extract metadata such as package name, version, dependencies, and source URLs. During this phase, only top-level variable assignments and expressions are evaluated—functions like `package()` are not executed.

In this PKGBUILD, all content consists of standard variable definitions (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `depends`, `source`, `sha256sums`) and does not include any command substitutions, function calls, or executable code at the global scope. The `source` array references a GitHub release asset through a proxy URL (`gh-proxy.com`), but this is still within the context of the official upstream (storytold/wordcraft), and using a proxy is not inherently malicious. The checksum is provided and matches the expected format, ensuring integrity verification later in the build process (though not evaluated during `--printsrcinfo`).

There is no evidence of obfuscated code, data exfiltration, or remote code execution triggered merely by sourcing the file. Therefore, running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>

No network operations, dynamic code execution, or suspicious commands are present in the build or package functions. All dependencies and metadata align with typical AUR packaging standards.

The use of a fixed version and checksum, along with the absence of runtime scripts or post-install hooks that modify the system beyond file installation, indicates a standard and safe packaging approach.
